content.text:
**Root cause** — `buildRouterOptions()` in `lib/route.js:616` used the user's `routerOptions` object *as* the target it filled in:

```js
const routerOptions = options.routerOptions || Object.create(null)
```

`processOptions()` shallow-copies the top-level options object, but not this nested one. So for every key in `routerKeys` that the user didn't set, Fastify wrote its own value straight into the caller's object — including `defaultRoute` and `onBadUrl`, which are closures created inside `fastify()` and bound to that one instance's `fourOhFour`/context. Reusing the same options object then gave instance #2 a router whose `defaultRoute` points at instance #1, and its 404 lookup hit instance #1's not-found context, which is `null` until that instance is readied — exactly the reported `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'server')` (`lib/four-oh-four.js:176`). That also explains why `app1.ready()` "fixed" it, and why the flat (deprecated) options never broke: nothing was written back into a shared object.

**Fix** — `lib/route.js:617` now builds a fresh null-prototype object per instance and leaves the caller's object untouched:

```js
const routerOptions = Object.assign(Object.create(null), options.routerOptions)
```

Explicit user values still win over top-level/deprecated options and defaults, so precedence is unchanged.

**Verification** — I reproduced the crash with a two-instance script before the change (`app2 /nope` threw the reported TypeError) and it returns a normal 404 afterwards. Added two regression tests in `test/router-options.test.js`: one asserting the user's `routerOptions` object keeps only its own keys, one building two instances from a shared options object and checking the second handles both its route and its own 404. `test/router-options.test.js` passes 34/34. Broader run (`node --test test/*.test.js test/internals/*.test.js`): 1926 pass, 1 fail — `test/plugin.4.test.js`, which fails to load because `@sinonjs/fake-timers` isn't installed in this worktree; pre-existing and unrelated. I couldn't run `eslint` or `borp` (permission denied for those commands), so the full suite and lint are unverified.

Per COMPLEX.md's co-change note for `lib/route.js`: I opened the partner `fastify.js` — `processOptions()` there is the only caller of `buildRouterOptions` and it already shallow-copies the outer options, so no change was needed on that side. Nothing committed.
